scenario-based software architecture (SA) evaluation methods are similar, but they differ in the activities, techniques, and stakeholders.

there is a common set of activities that are used in most of the studied SA evaluation methods, and that the studied methods are similar in their structure but differ in their activities and techniques.

the methods are structurally and partially similar but they have differences in terms of their activities and techniques; and the common activities among the methods can be used to construct a generic process model for SA evaluation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) to compare four scenario-based SA evaluation techniques, (2) to discover similarities and difference between the methods, and (3) to propose a generic process model for scenario-based SA evaluation.
the identification of a set of common activities and the definition of a process model to support scenario-based SA evaluation.
the comparison and analysis of scenario-based software architectures evaluation methods and the development of a generic process model.

the four methods share a number of commonalities but differ in the level of detail and formality.
there are similarities between the methods but also some important differences.
there are similarities and differences among existing scenario-based SA evaluation approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the studied methods have a common core that could be the starting point for a generic process model, but each method has a unique set of activities that make it different from others.
the studied methods are similar in structure and can be combined to form a generic process.
we have developed a framework that can be used to systematically compare scenario-based software architecture SA evaluation methods.

we have provided a systematic comparison of the studied evaluation methods.
